The structure is consistent: every book is represented by 5 consecutive lines (Title, Author, Publisher, Genre, Status), with occasional section headers that we should ignore.

Plan:
- Split the text into lines, strip whitespace
- Remove known headers/section labels
- Group remaining lines in chunks of 5 to form records
- Build a DataFrame and filter Author == Rick Riordan
- Count entries where Status != Available (i.e., Checked Out or Overdue)

```python
lines = [l.strip() for l in raw.split('\n') if l.strip()]

# Remove headers/section markers
headers = set([
    'Scribe County Public Library','Title','Author','Publisher','Genre','Status','Books',
    "Young Children's", 'Middle Grade', 'Young Adult', 'End of List'
])
filtered = [l for l in lines if l not in headers]

# Group into records of 5 lines each
records = [filtered[i:i+5] for i in range(0, len(filtered), 5)]
# Filter out any incomplete records defensively
records = [r for r in records if len(r) == 5]

cols = ['Title','Author','Publisher','Genre','Status']
df = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=cols)

riordan = df[df['Author'].str.lower().eq('rick riordan')]
not_on_shelves_status = {'checked out','overdue'}
riordan_not_on_shelves = riordan[riordan['Status'].str.lower().isin(not_on_shelves_status)]

print('Number of Rick Riordan books not currently on the library’s shelves:', len(riordan_not_on_shelves))
print('\nList of titles and their status:')
print(riordan_not_on_shelves[['Title','Status']].to_string(index=False))
```
